messages:
mike: Observed intermittent pod-to-pod timeouts for model-sync across us-west-2b -> us-west-2c, affecting GPU pools. P95 latency spikes, some KV sync fails. Anyone else?

sophia: seeing same, pods in namespace `gpu-serving` can't reach clusterIP svc for kv-sync intermittently. Errors look like TCP RSTs + icmp fragmentation? :thinking_face:

rajeev: tagging networking — did we push the new egress deny-by-default netpol last deploy?

mike: yes, roll 2026-03-18T03:22. netpol applied to gpu-serving with egress allowlist to serviceCIDR and dns. But cross-AZ pod cidrs not included? maybe serviceCIDR vs podCIDR confusion.

lee: quick check - run `kubectl -n gpu-serving get netpol -o yaml` then `ip route` on node? trying now

ops-bot: deploy 1864128800: netpol/gpu-egress updated by ci/infra-pipeline

sophia: output from `kubectl get netpol gpu-egress -n gpu-serving -o yaml` shows egress to `10.0.0.0/16` but our pod CIDRs are `10.1.0.0/16`, `10.2.0.0/16`, `10.3.0.0/16` across AZs. So netpol blocks cross-az pod->svc traffic that hairpins via node proxy.

mike: that would explain east-west failures. RDMA flows were trying preferred path but were falling back; logs showed MTU fragmentation and "ICMP frag needed" messages.

rajeev: temporary patch: adding a broader `ipBlock` to egress? e.g., `10.0.0.0/8` is risky. Better: add explicit pod CIDR ranges for AZs: `10.1.0.0/16`, `10.2.0.0/16`, `10.3.0.0/16`.

sophia: created PR to infra-configs to include podcidr list in netpol generator: https://git.company/redwood/infra-configs/pull/484 — linking for review.

lee: applied hotfix `kubectl apply -f hotfix-gpu-egress.yaml` to staging. That lifted errors for most pods. P95 latency dropped from ~240ms to ~28ms. :tada:

mike: for prod we need a safer policy: allow clusterIP svc range + nodeLocal lb range + podCIDR ranges. Also add an alert when netpol denies > 0 for `gpu-serving` namespace.

deploy-bot: rollout prod patch started by sophia — canary 10% (will coordinate with infra-sched)

sophia: note for postmortem — misread `serviceCIDR` vs actual pod ranges when hand-editing generator template. Add unit test to netpol generator to validate it includes all discovered pod CIDRs and service ranges.

rajeev: also FYI: RDMA sessions were dropping and falling back to TCP which increased CPU on inference nodes. Filed ticket INF-2124 to track perf regression.

mike: thanks everyone. I'll draft a short blameless postmortem + action items. Closing after prod stabilizes. :white_check_mark:
